key_insight: An MLIP-trained, CALPHAD-based workflow can rapidly map spinodal instability and predict resulting microstructure evolution across high-dimensional alloy composition spaces using analytic Gibbs energy derivatives.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more accurate screening of candidate alloys for spinodal microstructures, supporting composition-driven design of properties in complex multicomponent systems.
method: Use MLIP-derived elastic constants to estimate coherent strain contributions at scale.
Compute analytically derived Gibbs energy Hessians from CALPHAD models for stability analysis.
Feed the thermodynamic model into an elasto-chemical phase-field simulation to predict morphology.
evidence_signal: The workflow is demonstrated on the Hf-Nb-Ti-V quaternary system for microstructure stability analysis and visualization.
watch_item: Performance and predictive reliability may depend on the quality and transferability of the MLIP/CALPHAD models outside the demonstrated composition range.
paper_title: From MLIPs to Microstructure: A High-Throughput Computational Framework to Design Spinodal Alloys in High-Dimensional Composition Spaces via Analytic Derivatives of CALPHAD Model Predictions
